questions.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $2$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+2 & \le 10 \\ 4x+2-2 & \le 10-2 \\ 4x+0 & \le 8 \\ 4x & \le 8\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & \le 8 \\ \frac{4x}{4} & \le \frac{8}{4} \\ \frac{\cancel{4}x}{\cancel{4}} & \le 2 \\ x & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x\le 2.$

questions.problem: The solution to the inequality $-7t+2\le -5$ is $t${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $2$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-7t+2 & \le -5 \\ -7t+2-2 & \le -5-2 \\ -7t+0 & \le -7 \\ -7t & \le -7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-7.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-7t\,\, & \le \,\,-7 \\ \frac{-7t}{-7}\, & \ge \,\,\frac{-7}{-7} \\ \frac{\cancel{-7}t}{\cancel{-7}}\, & \ge \,\,1 \\ t\,\, & \ge \,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $t\ge 1.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose that we wish to find the solution to the inequality

$$
2x + 6 < 12.
$$

An inequality like this one can be solved just like an equation, using the addition and multiplication principles.

First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $6$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+6 & <12 \\ 2x+6-6 & <12-6 \\ 2x+0 & <6 \\ 2x & <6\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $2{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & <6 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & <\frac{6}{2} \\ \frac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{2}} & <3 \\ x & <3\end{aligned}
$$

The solution is $x < 3$ In other words, any value less than $3$ satisfies the inequality.

Let's see another example.
